name: Apple-Cider Glazed Pork Chops with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Jasmine Rice
description: Thick pork chops seared hard, then finished in a quick pan glaze of apple cider, Dijon, and honey. Brussels sprouts roast and rice simmers while the chops cook, so everything lands at the same time.
ingredients: 1.5 lb brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Pull the pork chops out of the fridge, pat dry, and season both sides with most of the salt and the pepper.
Rinse the jasmine rice, then bring to a boil with the 2.25 cups water and a pinch of salt. Cover, drop to low, and cook 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave covered.
Toss the brussels sprouts with 2 Tbsp olive oil and the rest of the salt. Spread cut-side down on a sheet pan and roast 20–25 minutes, until browned and tender.
Heat the remaining 1 Tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear the chops about 4 minutes per side, until 140°F inside. Move to a plate.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the cider, scraping up the browned bits. Whisk in the Dijon and honey and simmer about 6 minutes, until reduced by half and syrupy.
Swirl in the butter, return the chops and any juices, and spoon glaze over them for a minute until they hit 145°F. Rest 3 minutes, then serve with the rice and brussels sprouts.
tips: Start the rice and sprouts first; the chops and glaze only take about 15 minutes.
Thinner chops need just 2–3 minutes per side.
No cider on hand? Apple juice plus a splash of cider vinegar works.
